- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline at 10–15% below peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.15) over 5+ days, model underestimates upside — add 2–5% to forecast mean.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — adjust downward by 3–7% for first 7 days.
- When sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model often fails to reverse trend — add a 1–3% downward bias starting from day 10.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is > 10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- Sentiment volatility > 0.3 in last 5 days → model overfits noise → reduce forecast variance by 10–20% in next 7 days.
